source.title: GDP deflators at market prices, and money GDP October 2026 (Budget)
source.edition: October 2026 (Budget) - published 29 October 2026; outturn to 2025-26 from ONS Quarterly National Accounts 30 September 2026 (series L8GG), forecasts 2026-27 to 2031-32 from the OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook, 28 October 2026

academic_year_method: An academic year Sept Y to Aug Y+1 (the AAR year 'Y/YY') has 7 months in financial year Y-(Y+1) (Sept-Mar) and 5 months in financial year (Y+1)-(Y+2) (Apr-Aug), so its index is (7 x FY[Y-(Y+1)] + 5 x FY[(Y+1)-(Y+2)]) / 12, on the same base (financial year 2025-26 = 100). This is the usual 7/12 + 5/12 month-share way of moving between financial and academic years, and keeps academy (AAR) and council-school (CFR) figures on one consistent deflator. 'part_forecast' means the later financial year is an OBR forecast. Cross-checked against a month-weighted average of ONS quarterly L8GG (Sep from Q3 Y; Q4 Y; Q1 and Q2 Y+1; Jul-Aug from Q3 Y+1): see academic_year_quarterly_check. The two agree within about 0.13 per cent except 2019/20 (-0.9 per cent), 2020/21 (+1.2), 2021/22 (+0.4) and 2022/23 (-0.6), where the quarterly deflator swung sharply (the COVID spike to 84.99 in 2020 Q2, then the 2022 inflation surge) and the annual financial-year averages smooth it. The 7/12 + 5/12 series is preferred for the site because it is smooth, covers forecast years and matches the financial-year series that HMT and the IFS publish.

academic_year_quarterly_check.description: Month-weighted ONS L8GG quarterly index (QNA 30 Sep 2026) for each academic year it covers, and the per cent by which academic_years differs from it. Quarterly data stop at 2026 Q2, so 2024/25 is the last year checked.

ifs_november_2025_edition.description: HM Treasury GDP deflators, November 2025 (Budget 2025) edition - the edition the IFS 2025-26 annual report on education spending in England uses - rebased from 2024-25 = 100 to 2025-26 = 100 so it sits on the same base. In that edition 2025-26 itself was an OBR forecast (+2.943 per cent on 2024-25). Use it only to reproduce or compare with IFS figures; the main series above is newer (later ONS revisions, 2025-26 is outturn).

notes: Whole-economy GDP deflator at market prices, financial years April-March, indexed 2025-26 = 100. The October 2026 workbook is already on a 2025-26 = 100 base, so outturn values (2010-11 to 2025-26) are copied from column C (4 dp, as published). The workbook prints '-' for forecast index values and gives only the per cent change on the previous year (column D), so forecast years (status 'forecast') are built by chaining those changes from 2025-26 = 100 and are OBR projections, not outturn. HMT's financial-year values equal the mean of the four ONS quarterly L8GG values (Q2 Y to Q1 Y+1); that was verified for every year from 2010-11 to 2025-26 (all within 0.0001). To express a cash amount in 2025-26 prices: real = cash x 100 / index[year] (use financial_years for CFR years like '2023-24' and academic_years for AAR years like '2023/24'). This is the measure HM Treasury and the IFS use for real-terms public spending; it reflects whole-economy prices, not school costs (teacher pay, energy), which DfE/IFS sometimes track separately as a school-specific cost index. The series is revised each quarter as ONS revises GDP: the next HMT update follows the ONS Quarterly National Accounts of 22 December 2026, and real-terms figures will shift slightly then.
